svg.title: Phase 1 dataset creation plan
svg.desc: Detailed breakdown of dataset schema, query taxonomy, data sources, generation pipeline, and daily tasks for the NH White Mountains hiking agent

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How should I structure the trail fact sheet JSON?')
g.text: Trail fact sheets — the ground truth
One structured JSON record per trail; every Q&A pair is grounded in these

svg.text: Scope: ~80 trails
· All 48 NH 4,000-footers (required — the explicit user objective)
· ~30 build-up / approach hikes: lower peaks, ridge walks, hut approaches (e.g. Lonesome Lake, Welch-Dickey)
· Fields per trail: name, peak(s), region, distance, elevation gain, highest point, difficulty rating (1–5),
trailhead GPS, recommended seasons, typical time range, notable hazards, gear tiers, AMC hut nearby
· Difficulty rating must encode both fitness demand AND technical demand separately — critical for progressions
· Tag each trail: above-treeline exposure, water crossings, scrambling, winter-viable, family-friendly

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Walk me through the query taxonomy in detail')
g.text: Query taxonomy — 5 types, all must be represented
Roughly equal distribution across types; progression queries need the most examples

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Give me 5 example trail lookup queries for the dataset')
sendPrompt('Give me 5 example trail recommendation queries for the dataset')
sendPrompt('Give me 5 example progression planning queries for the dataset')
sendPrompt('Give me 5 example gear and safety queries for the dataset')
sendPrompt('Give me 5 example weather and conditions queries for the dataset')
sendPrompt('Show me a full example JSONL training record')
g.text: Training record schema — JSONL, one object per line
Chat format compatible with most SFT frameworks (TRL, Unsloth, Axolotl)

svg.text: Required fields
· system — fixed hiking agent persona + scope statement (same across all records)
· user — the query; vary phrasing, length, formality (beginner casual vs. expert terse)
· assistant — the ideal response; structured but conversational, safety note where warranted
Metadata fields (stripped before training, kept for QA)
· query_type — one of the 5 types above
· trail_refs — list of trail IDs this record draws from (for traceability)
· difficulty — beginner / intermediate / expert (for stratified eval split)
· reviewed — bool; no unreviewed record goes into the training split

g.onclick: sendPrompt('What data sources should I use for the White Mountains trail facts?')
g.text: Data sources — for seeding trail fact sheets
Use these to populate fields; do not copy text verbatim into training examples

svg.text: · AMC White Mountain Guide (distances, times, technical notes) — authoritative
· USFS White Mountain National Forest trail data (trailhead coords, parking, fees)
· NEHH / 4000footers.com (official 4K footer list, completion criteria)
· Mt. Washington Observatory (historical weather windows, seasonal hazard data)
· AllTrails / Peakbagger for cross-checking distances and elevation gain figures
· AMC hut system pages for hut proximity, services, and reservation info

g.onclick: sendPrompt('Walk me through the LLM-assisted generation pipeline in detail')
g.text: Treat the frontier LLM as a fast first-draft writer, not the source of truth

svg.text: Populate trail fact JSON for all ~80 trails from sources above
Write a generation prompt: "given this trail fact sheet, generate N Q&A pairs of type X"
Run Claude / GPT-4o over all trails; output directly as JSONL with metadata fields
Review pass: verify distances, elevations, trailheads; flag & fix safety-critical errors
Split: 85% train / 10% eval / 5% held-out test; stratify by query type and difficulty

g.onclick: sendPrompt('How do I calculate how many examples I need per trail and query type?')
g.text: ~6–8 per trail on avg · progression queries need 2–3× more variation · quality > quantity
